tex_content.html:
Proof

↗ A_0 ↗ stdsoln ↗ prop:surgery-cap-evolution-alternative ↗ posdistdec ↗ stdsolncannbhd ↗ canonvary ↗ neckglue ↗ def:overline-delta-0 ↗ Restim \sketch

The cap curvature bound gives a uniform lower bound

\begin{equation} \bar h_a^2\geq (2D'D)^{-1} \end{equation}

for the surgery scale. Claim 2 bounds $t_a/\bar h_a^2<1$. Standard-solution compactness then places a uniformly large ball around $x_a$ inside the evolved cap. The standard canonical-neighborhood theorem gives either a cap or an evolving neck. A cap transfers directly by smooth convergence; in the neck case, its initial slice lies in the continuing region and Proposition neckglue glues it to the surgery neck. Both cases contradict failure of the canonical-neighborhood assumption.

□

dependencies.title: stdsoln
dependencies.description:
\label{stdsoln}

A standard Ricci flow exists. Every standard flow $(\Ar^3,g(t))$, $0\le t<T$,
is unique, has $T=1$, is complete with strictly positive curvature for
$0<t<1$, is $SO(3)$-invariant, is asymptotic on every $[0,t_0]$, $t_0<1$,
to $(S^2,h(t))\times\Ar$ with $R_{h(t)}=(1-t)^{-1}$, and is
$\kappa$-noncollapsed below some scale $r>0$.
\end{theorem}

stdsolncannbhd
dependencies.description:
\label{stdsolncannbhd}

For every $\epsilon>0$ there is $C'(\epsilon)<\infty$ such that every
$(x,t)$ lies either in the core of a $(C',\epsilon)$-cap, at the center
of an evolving $\epsilon$-neck starting at $0$ and initially disjoint from
the surgery cap, or at the center of an evolving $\epsilon$-neck defined
for rescaled time $1+\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}
